name: co.internationalcall/dialing
title: InternationalCall.co dialing
description: Dialing instructions, call prices, and the numbers organisations publish for callers abroad.

tools.name: get_dialing_instructions
tools.description: Exact digits to dial a phone in another country from the caller's country: exit code, country code, and the national number with its trunk prefix correctly dropped or kept, plus the + form for mobiles and numbered steps. Use it for any "how do I call this country or number" question, including shared-code zones (the US, Canada and most of the Caribbean dial 1 + ten digits, with no exit code). For what the call costs, use get_call_price instead. Pass `number` for that number's exact sequence (a + international number needs nothing else; a local-format number also needs `destination`), or only `destination` for the country's rule and a real example. `origin` defaults to the US. Derived from Google's libphonenumber metadata.

destination.description: Country being called: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "MX", or an English name such as "Mexico".

origin.description: Country the caller is dialing from (default "US"): an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "MX", or an English name such as "Mexico".

number.description: A specific phone number, as the caller has it: local format ("55 1234 5678", needs destination) or international ("+52 55 1234 5678").

tools.name: get_call_price
tools.description: Per-minute price of calling a country, or a specific number, from a web browser with InternationalCall.co: the live rate, how billing works (prepaid credit, no subscription), and a link that opens the dialer set to that country. Use it when someone asks what a call abroad costs or how to call a phone abroad from a computer. For which digits to dial, use get_dialing_instructions instead. Pass `destination` for the country's standard rate, or `number` to price that exact number: premium, satellite-adjacent and special-service ranges cost more than the standard rate (a local-format number also needs `destination`). The rate depends only on the number called, not on where the caller is.

destination.description: Country being called: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "MX", or an English name such as "Mexico".

number.description: A specific phone number, as the caller has it: local format ("55 1234 5678", needs destination) or international ("+52 55 1234 5678").

tools.name: find_number_for_callers_abroad
tools.description: The phone number a tax office, pension or benefits agency, immigration service, bank, student loan servicer or phone carrier publishes for people calling from OUTSIDE its country (domestic short codes, 0800/1-800 and 0300-style numbers mostly do not connect from abroad), as read on the organisation's own website, with its published hours and time zone, the source page, and a link that opens a browser dialer with the number filled in. Pass `organisation` ("HMRC", "Wells Fargo", "National Pension Service", "Kela") and optionally `country` to narrow it, or only `country` to list what is covered there. For how to dial a number use get_dialing_instructions; for what a call costs use get_call_price.

organisation.description: The organisation, as people call it ("HMRC", "Social Security", "Banco BHD", "Kela"), or the kind of office when the name is not known ("tax office", "pension", "health insurance", "consulate", "passport", "student loan", "bank", "airline"); pair it with `country`.

country.description: The organisation's country: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "MX", or an English name such as "Mexico".
